text:
Maria K: quick q — for routing policies + quota enforcement: should overridable per-customer policy live in the same UI as per-tier defaults? thinking about complexity for support. /cc @Ajay P

Ajay P: I'd prefer tier defaults + customer overrides. simpler to reason if we define merge precedence: customer > team > tier. :thumbsup:

Taylor W: merging is fine but telemetry/alerting gets tricky. If customer override routes to expensive model variant, we need per-customer token burn metrics in the console and per-route latency breakdowns.

Oliver S: also consider atomicity when applying quota checks + fallback. current flow: check quota -> route -> serve. race if two concurrent requests dip negative. we should enforce quota using an atomic token reservation in the router.

Ajay P: agree. API proposal snippet:

```
policy: {
  defaults: { tier: "pro", max_qps: 10 },
  overrides: [ { customer_id: "acct_123", max_qps: 50, route: ["gpt-q4", "gpt-q2a"] } ]
}
```

Maria K: that helps. how does fallback variant ordering work when quota exhausted? e.g. fall back to q2a vs smaller model in other region.

Taylor W: fallback should be a deterministic ordered list with costs + latency metadata. router picks first variant with available quota in preferred region, else next. we need console UX to show effective list per-customer (calculated merge) and simulation mode.

Oliver S: Simulation mode is huge for support onboarding. also need audit logs for each decision (policy id, evaluated rules, chosen variant, reason).

deploy-bot: rollout started for policy-service v2 (canary 10%) :rocket:

Ajay P: last thought — quota enforcement windows: per-second token reservations + per-minute billing buckets. prevents bursty denial while still tracking cost.

Maria K: ok, I'll sketch console screens: effective policy panel, override editor, and "simulate traffic" button. will share mock tomorrow. :wave:
